sources.title: Steplight AI non-diagnostic task-initiation design principles
sources.note: Original product guidance: one optional next action, gentle capacity fit, no diagnosis or pressure.

sources.title: The Fogg Behavior Model
sources.note: General behavior-design framing; entries use original wording and are not treatment advice.

sources.title: Implementation intentions: Strong effects of simple plans
sources.note: Bibliographic source for simple if-then planning; no source text is reproduced.

sources.title: Cognitive load during problem solving: Effects on learning
sources.note: Bibliographic source for reducing unnecessary task complexity; no clinical claims are made.

strategies.name: Open one relevant material
strategies.use_case: Starting study, research, paperwork, or a project when several files or sources feel hard to approach.
strategies.sample: Open the one document or resource most related to this task.
strategies.caution: Opening is enough; do not require reading or finishing it now.

source_metadata.basis: One visible, optional first action.
Reduce the effort needed to begin.

strategies.name: Write one rough sentence
strategies.use_case: Beginning an essay, email, report, application, or blank-page writing task.
strategies.sample: Write one rough sentence about what this piece needs to say.
strategies.caution: A fragment or placeholder counts; editing is not required.

source_metadata.basis: Make the first move small and non-perfectionistic.
Limit simultaneous decisions at the start.

strategies.name: Name a physical first move
strategies.use_case: Tasks that feel vague, large, or difficult to translate into an immediate action.
strategies.sample: Name one physical action that could begin this task.
strategies.caution: Choose an action, not a full plan or a judgment about progress.

source_metadata.basis: Translate a broad intention into one tiny next action.
Use concrete action wording.

strategies.name: Make a gentle if-then cue
strategies.use_case: A task with a known place, time, or trigger but an uncertain start.
strategies.sample: Finish the sentence: “When I am at my workspace, I can first…”
strategies.caution: Keep the cue flexible; it is not a promise or deadline.

source_metadata.basis: Original if-then cue, adapted as optional planning.
Avoid pressure and preserve user choice.

strategies.name: Put one needed tool within reach
strategies.use_case: Hands-on, creative, cooking, repair, or household work that requires a specific tool.
strategies.sample: Place one tool needed for this task where you can see it.
strategies.caution: Gather only one item; preparation can stop there.

source_metadata.basis: Make a first action easier to do.
One action is a complete stopping point.

strategies.name: Open the task workspace
strategies.use_case: Starting computer, design, coding, or administrative work that has a familiar app or workspace.
strategies.sample: Open the app or workspace used for this task.
strategies.caution: No further work is expected after opening it.

source_metadata.basis: Reduce startup friction.
Keep the first move bounded.

strategies.name: Write the first question
strategies.use_case: Research, troubleshooting, studying, or planning when the goal is not yet clear.
strategies.sample: Write one question you would like this task to answer.
strategies.caution: The question may be incomplete; answers can wait.

source_metadata.basis: Narrow the immediate decision space.
Use a gentle, non-diagnostic prompt.

strategies.name: Read one heading
strategies.use_case: Approaching a long reading, study, policy, or technical document.
strategies.sample: Read one heading in the material for this task.
strategies.caution: There is no requirement to continue to the next section.

source_metadata.basis: Present one small unit at a time.
Make stopping after one action acceptable.

strategies.name: Mark one relevant item
strategies.use_case: Reviewing notes, a checklist, research, or a document with several details.
strategies.sample: Mark one line or item that looks relevant to the task.
strategies.caution: Do not try to organize or annotate everything at once.

source_metadata.basis: Offer one observable action.
Limit the amount of material handled at once.

strategies.name: Write three temporary labels
strategies.use_case: Outlining a report, presentation, project, or study notes when some planning capacity is available.
strategies.sample: Write up to three rough labels for parts of the task.
strategies.caution: Labels are placeholders, not a commitment to complete every part.

source_metadata.basis: Externalize a small amount of structure.
Keep planning proportionate to capacity.

strategies.name: Draft one bullet
strategies.use_case: Writing, meeting preparation, reports, or presentations when a single idea can get the work moving.
strategies.sample: Add one rough bullet to the place where this task belongs.
strategies.caution: A rough bullet is enough; do not expand it unless you choose to.

source_metadata.basis: Single optional writing action.
Make the response small and actionable.

strategies.name: Save the current draft
strategies.use_case: Writing, coding, design, or document work where preserving current progress is the next useful action.
strategies.sample: Save the current file once.
strategies.caution: Saving does not mean the work is finished or ready to share.

source_metadata.basis: Offer a useful, bounded action at any capacity.
Make the desired action easy to complete.

strategies.name: Run one focused check
strategies.use_case: Coding or technical work with a specific test, command, or expected behavior.
strategies.sample: Run one test related to the part you just changed.
strategies.caution: A failure is information; it does not require fixing everything now.

source_metadata.basis: Keep verification targeted and non-punitive.
Focus attention on one unit of work.

strategies.name: Read one error message
strategies.use_case: Debugging or troubleshooting when an error feels like too much to investigate at once.
strategies.sample: Read the first error message and note one unfamiliar word.
strategies.caution: Understanding one message is enough; no fix is required yet.

source_metadata.basis: Isolate one piece of troubleshooting information.
Separate noticing from solving.

strategies.name: Create one placeholder file
strategies.use_case: Starting coding, writing, or digital projects where an empty workspace is a barrier.
strategies.sample: Create one clearly named empty file for this task.
strategies.caution: A placeholder is sufficient; it does not need content yet.

source_metadata.basis: Make a concrete first action available.
Reduce the blank-start barrier without pressure.

strategies.name: Choose one reference
strategies.use_case: Research or study tasks with many sources, tabs, books, or links.
strategies.sample: Choose one reference to keep open for this task.
strategies.caution: Do not compare every source or build a complete bibliography now.

source_metadata.basis: Reduce competing inputs.
One choice is a complete first action.

strategies.name: Capture one useful fact
strategies.use_case: Study, research, or preparation when a small amount of information can anchor the next move.
strategies.sample: Write down one fact you already know about the subject.
strategies.caution: Recall can be partial; checking sources may come later.

source_metadata.basis: Start from available knowledge, not an exhaustive plan.
Keep the information unit small.

strategies.name: Sort up to three items
strategies.use_case: Tidying a desk, shelf, inbox, or small household area when a visible boundary is helpful.
strategies.sample: Put up to three obvious items where they belong.
strategies.caution: Stop at three or sooner; the surrounding area can remain as it is.

source_metadata.basis: Use a bounded action and an easy stop.
Reduce the effort of starting.

strategies.name: Clear one small surface
strategies.use_case: Household organization or cleaning where the whole room or area feels too large.
strategies.sample: Clear one small, visible patch of the surface.
strategies.caution: A small patch is the whole task for now; do not expand the boundary automatically.

source_metadata.basis: Keep household actions visually bounded.
Avoid adding unrelated subtasks.

strategies.name: Prepare one laundry load
strategies.use_case: Laundry tasks when sorting, washing, drying, and putting away feel like one large job.
strategies.sample: Put one suitable group of clothes into the washer.
strategies.caution: Starting a load does not require folding or putting away other clothes.

source_metadata.basis: Separate one stage from the rest of a household task.
Make the first action concrete.

strategies.name: Wash one dish
strategies.use_case: Kitchen cleanup or dishes when a full sink or kitchen feels difficult to approach.
strategies.sample: Wash or rinse one dish and let that be enough.
strategies.caution: This is not a request to finish the sink or clean the kitchen.

source_metadata.basis: One finite household action with permission to stop.
Lower the effort threshold for beginning.

strategies.name: Prepare one ingredient
strategies.use_case: Cooking or meal preparation when the recipe has several ingredients and steps.
strategies.sample: Take out and prepare one ingredient for the meal.
strategies.caution: Follow ordinary food-safety guidance; you can stop after this ingredient.

source_metadata.basis: Break meal preparation into one optional action.
Handle one input at a time.

strategies.name: Draft a short update
strategies.use_case: Communication or work coordination when an update is needed but composing a complete message feels hard.
strategies.sample: Draft one sentence describing the current status.
strategies.caution: Review recipients and details before sending; drafting alone is enough.

source_metadata.basis: Offer a small, reversible communication step.
Use a concrete action cue.

strategies.name: Acknowledge one message
strategies.use_case: Email or messaging backlogs where a simple acknowledgment can clarify the next step.
strategies.sample: Draft a brief acknowledgment for one message.
strategies.caution: Check the context and recipient before sending; no reply is required if it is not appropriate.

source_metadata.basis: Keep communication bounded and under user control.
Handle one message rather than the whole inbox.

strategies.name: Complete one form field
strategies.use_case: Applications, forms, or official paperwork with many required fields.
strategies.sample: Complete one field whose answer you already know.
strategies.caution: Do not submit until the form has been checked for accuracy.

source_metadata.basis: Make paperwork progress one field at a time.
Lower friction for one action.

strategies.name: Find one relevant date
strategies.use_case: Bills, appointments, applications, or admin tasks where a date is needed before acting.
strategies.sample: Find one date or reference number needed for this task.
strategies.caution: Use the original source to verify details before making a payment or submission.

source_metadata.basis: Make a single information-gathering action.
Avoid processing the entire admin task at once.

strategies.name: Write one call detail
strategies.use_case: Preparing for an appointment, service call, or conversation with a specific organization.
strategies.sample: Write down the one detail you want to remember for the call.
strategies.caution: This is preparation only; choosing whether and when to call remains yours.

source_metadata.basis: Support preparation without forcing contact.
Clarify a possible next action.

strategies.name: Create a short outline
strategies.use_case: Reports, lessons, presentations, or project plans when capacity allows a little structure.
strategies.sample: Write two or three rough headings for the work.
strategies.caution: Keep the outline provisional; it is not a contract to complete every section.

source_metadata.basis: Externalize a small amount of structure.
Keep scope gentle and adjustable.

strategies.name: Choose one subtask
strategies.use_case: Large multi-part projects when there is enough energy to select a starting area.
strategies.sample: Choose one part of the project to look at first.
strategies.caution: Choosing does not mean the other parts are less important.

source_metadata.basis: Choose one next action from a larger goal.
Improve action clarity and ability.
